FreeMarker and Thymeleaf for Java applications

Colibri supplies the component templates. Your Java application supplies the template engine. The browser loads Colibri CSS and JavaScript after the server renders the page.

1. Add your template engine

In a Spring Boot application, choose the starter you use. Your existing Spring Boot dependency management supplies its version.

<dependency>
  <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
  <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-freemarker</artifactId>
</dependency>
<!-- OR: spring-boot-starter-thymeleaf -->

Maven downloads FreeMarker or Thymeleaf and its dependencies. Colibri’s resource JAR does not bundle either engine.

2. Add Colibri’s templates

Download the template JAR

Source and Java tests on GitHub · Thymeleaf fragments · FreeMarker macros

Install the downloaded JAR in your local Maven repository:

mvn install:install-file \
  -Dfile=colibri-templates-0.1.0.jar \
  -DgroupId=ai.l3v.colibri \
  -DartifactId=colibri-templates \
  -Dversion=0.1.0 -Dpackaging=jar

From the Colibri checkout, build the supplemental JAR:

mvn -f java/colibri-templates/pom.xml clean install
<dependency>
  <groupId>ai.l3v.colibri</groupId>
  <artifactId>colibri-templates</artifactId>
  <version>0.1.0</version>
</dependency>

This artifact is installed locally by the command above; it is not published to Maven Central. You can also copy the freemarker/ or thymeleaf/ directory into your application’s src/main/resources/templates/colibri/ directory.

3. Render components with model data

FreeMarker

[#ftl output_format="HTML"]
[#import "/colibri/freemarker/ui.ftl" as ui]
[@ui.button disabled=saving]${buttonLabel}[/@ui.button]

Use .ftlh for Spring Boot’s default HTML template suffix, or configure your application’s suffix. HTML auto-escaping stays enabled.

Thymeleaf

<button th:replace="~{colibri/thymeleaf/button :: button(${buttonLabel}, 'outline', ${saving})}"></button>

Native fragments bind model values, iterate collections and conditionally render content. The Spring field fragment supports th:field, rejected values and validation errors. No custom dialect is required.

4. Serve the browser assets

Serve Colibri’s src/ and themes/ under your application’s static /ui/ path. Link /ui/themes/colibri.css, put class="ui-root" on the app root and load /ui/src/core/auto.js as a module. The template JAR contains server templates, not these browser assets.
